**New retrospective analysis.** July 26, 2023 is a coverage label, not a
work or publication date. The analysis ran on November 24, 2026 at 12:13:50
UTC-08:00. This draft has not been published; its publication date is unknown.

## The question

Which months saw the largest month-to-month movements in the average price
levels of bread, eggs and milk, considered separately?

The original workbooks contain monthly U.S. city average prices from January
2018 through May 2023, from the **June 13, 2023 ALFRED vintage**. The files
were created in November 2026. This fixed vintage does not necessarily
include everything available by the July coverage date.

## Within each series

For each product, the analysis subtracts the previous month's price from the
current price. Absolute change is the magnitude of that difference; percentage
change divides the signed difference by the previous price. Each series has
65 observations and 64 consecutive comparisons. The first month has no prior
observation, so its differences are blank. The workbook audit stops on missing
data; the calculation also marks unavailable comparisons rather than bridging
a missing month or value.

The largest absolute movement **within each product** is shown below. The
units differ, so the rows are not a ranking across products.

| Product | Month | Signed change | Absolute change | Percentage change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| White bread | September 2021 | +$0.113 per pound | $0.113 per pound | +7.70% |
| Large eggs | March 2023 | -$0.765 per dozen | $0.765 per dozen | -18.17% |
| Whole milk | May 2022 | +$0.192 per gallon | $0.192 per gallon | +4.79% |

The [monthly differences table](grocery-2023-07-26-assets/monthly-differences.csv)
contains the prices, units, differences and comparison status for every
observation. These changes describe average price levels, **not formal CPI
inflation measures**. They are national urban averages, not local store
prices; the [BLS recommends CPI indexes](https://www.bls.gov/cpi/factsheets/average-prices.htm)
for measuring price change.
